source.title: Understanding Grokking Through A Robustness Viewpoint

record.tranche_reason: The study measures grokking on modular addition and MNIST and compares standard training with perturbation-based training, but its main method and focus differ from the original grokking studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own train/test accuracy curves on MNIST and modular addition, plus an abelian-degrok training result. Its discussion of grokking results from prior work is not recorded as findings. It also reports robustness metrics and abelian-test results that relate to grokking but do not measure the behaviors named by V1 or V3; these are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The paper reports its own train/test accuracy curves showing grokking on modular addition (P=113, 30% train fraction, Nanda et al. setup) and on MNIST (Omnigrok setup). Its aim is a robustness explanation and perturbation-based speed-ups, not a replication of the original measurements.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also stress that standard training does not learn the commutative law before grokking. They attribute the perturbation method's speed-up to learning that law. The 'sufficient condition' result is a theoretical bound under assumptions; empirically, they note weight norm does not track the test jump in a timely way.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the same broad grokking tasks and train/test accuracy behavior, but focuses on robustness, adds perturbation-based training, and follows cited setups for MNIST and modulo addition rather than reporting an explicit replication of the original study. It uses a 30% training fraction for modulo addition and does not vary training-set size.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports different perturbation strengths for MNIST and modulo addition and adaptive strength based on training accuracy. The information metrics use different perturbation strengths by dataset; the paper also varies matrix entropy order α in an ablation.

fits_no_version.finding: Adaptive Gaussian input or embedding perturbation during training shortens the grokking delay on MNIST and on modular addition. A commutativity regularizer shortens it further on modular addition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input-perturbation (augmentation-like) training reduces or removes the grokking delay.

fits_no_version.finding: Perturbation error falls after train accuracy saturates, and sharpness falls continuously. The l2 weight norm drops before the test-accuracy jump.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Robustness-related measures and weight norm track or precede grokking.

fits_no_version.finding: Perturbed mutual information and entropy change sharply at the test-accuracy jump. Their perturbed-versus-unperturbed differences are small, or fall, before train accuracy saturates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Matrix-information robustness metrics correlate with grokking and are hypothesized predictors.

fits_no_version.finding: Under standard training, the modular-addition model fails the commutativity test on training data until it groks. Under perturbation training it passes right after train accuracy saturates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning commutativity coincides with grokking on modular addition.

record.problems: Reported curves and several results are figure-only, with no numerical accuracy or timing values or uncertainty estimates. No training-set-size sweep is reported. The proposed prediction metrics are not validated as predictions; the authors describe them as hypotheses or potential predictors.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 3 reports a constructed predicted-accuracy curve that the text says closely matches real test accuracy; it is an illustration based on assumed parameters and a modeled distance distribution, not a separate training result. Figures 7 and 12 and Figure 13 concern representation/logit distance or metric ablations rather than a versioned behavior and are not included as rows.

untested.parts: Whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks: only a 30% training fraction is used. No numbers on chance-level start or timing of the jump.
No circuit identification, no measure of memorization removal, no test of gradual circuit formation.
Text and molecules are not tested. No manipulation of initialization scale or weight norm to switch grokking on or off.
No efficiency comparison, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
No comparison of algorithms across runs.
Optimizer and floating-point artifacts are not controlled; AdamW is used throughout.

record.verdict_notes: All grokking evidence is figure-only, with no numbers, seeds or uncertainty. Figure 3 is a fitted theoretical curve with hand-chosen parameters, correctly left out. The study is not one of the original sources.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare training-set sizes or report whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks.
Does not identify a Fourier or other generalizing circuit, measure removal of memorizing components, or test whether such a circuit forms gradually.
Tests MNIST as an image task, but not text or molecules, nor initialization scale, weight norm, or a lazy-to-rich transition.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data.
Does not test whether low norm favors an efficient circuit, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below it.
Does not compare identifiable algorithms across runs, architectures, or hyperparameters.
Does not test adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point/softmax artifacts, or control for them.
